challenges.intro_fact: Organic September is a good moment to ask what 'organic' actually means, and whether it makes the difference people assume.

questions.text: Ireland's national strategy targets what share of agricultural land to be farmed organically by 2030?
questions.fact: Ireland's organic strategy targets 10% of agricultural land to be farmed organically by 2030, up from a much smaller base today, as part of the country's wider CAP Strategic Plan.

questions.text: The EU's Farm to Fork Strategy sets a target for organic farming across the bloc by 2030. What is it?
questions.fact: The EU's Farm to Fork Strategy targets at least 25% of agricultural land to be farmed organically by 2030, more than double Ireland's own national target.

questions.text: Meta-analyses of organic farming have found what effect on farmland biodiversity, compared to conventional farming?
options: Fewer species due to lower yields
Only affects soil microbes, not visible wildlife
questions.fact: Meta-analyses comparing organic and conventional farms have found organic farms host roughly 30% more species on average, from pollinators to birds, largely due to lower pesticide and fertiliser use.

challenges.action_intro: You don't need to switch your whole shop to organic to make a difference.

actions.title: Try one organic swap in your weekly shop
actions.desc: Pick one item, maybe your fruit and veg, and go organic for a week.

actions.title: Look for the EU organic logo when shopping
actions.desc: The green leaf logo means the product meets strict EU organic farming standards.
actions.carbon: Helps identify verified organic produce quickly

challenges.resources: Teagasc organic farming: teagasc.ie | EU Farm to Fork Strategy: food.ec.europa.eu | Organic Trust Ireland: organictrust.ie

challenges.intro_fact: September is peak back-to-school traffic. A growing number of Irish schools are trying to make the school run less car-dependent.

questions.text: What is Ireland's programme that funds safer walking and cycling routes for kids getting to school called?
questions.fact: The Safe Routes to School programme funds infrastructure like cycle paths, footpaths and reduced-traffic zones around Irish schools, part of a wider push to make active travel to school the norm.

questions.text: In the Netherlands, roughly what share of all trips are made by bicycle, one of the highest rates in the world?
questions.fact: Around 27% of all trips in the Netherlands are made by bike, among the highest cycling rates in the world, thanks to decades of investment in dedicated cycling infrastructure.

questions.text: A major European study on travel habits found that people who cycle regularly have daily travel carbon footprints how much lower than non-cyclists?
questions.fact: A major European study (Brand et al., 2021) found that people who cycle regularly have daily travel carbon footprints around 84% lower than those who don't, even accounting for the other trips they make.

challenges.action_intro: September is peak back-to-school traffic, a good week to try something different.

actions.title: Walk or cycle the school run at least once this week
actions.desc: Even one day makes a difference to both traffic and air quality outside the school gates.
actions.carbon: Cuts short-trip car emissions near schools

actions.title: Check if there's a Safe Routes scheme near your school
actions.desc: See what's planned or already built nearby, and support it if there's a local consultation.

challenges.resources: Safe Routes to School: gov.ie | Green-Schools Ireland: greenschoolsireland.org | IrishCycle.com

challenges.intro_fact: Heating is one of Ireland's most overlooked climate problems, and unlike most sectors, its emissions have actually been rising.

questions.text: Roughly what share of Ireland's total greenhouse gas emissions comes from heating buildings?
questions.fact: Heating accounts for nearly a quarter of Ireland's national emissions, and emissions here have actually been rising since 2014, according to the SEAI National Heat Study.

questions.text: What fuel source still dominates home heating in Ireland?
questions.fact: Home heating in Ireland is still dominated by oil, one of the highest-emitting ways to heat a home, and progress switching away from it has been slower than planned.

questions.text: How much more efficient is a typical heat pump compared to a standard oil or electric heater?
options: Heat pumps are less efficient in cold climates
questions.fact: A well-installed heat pump typically delivers 3 to 4 units of heat for every 1 unit of electricity it uses, making it far more efficient than oil boilers, even in cooler climates.

challenges.action_intro: A few small fixes now save money and emissions once the heating season kicks in properly.

actions.title: Check your attic and wall insulation
actions.desc: Poor insulation is one of the biggest reasons Irish homes waste heat. SEAI grants can cover a large share of upgrade costs.
actions.carbon: Cuts heat loss and heating-related emissions

actions.title: Bleed your radiators before the cold sets in
actions.desc: Trapped air makes radiators work harder for less heat. A five-minute job.

challenges.resources: SEAI home energy grants: seai.ie | SEAI National Heat Study: seai.ie | gov.ie Climate Action Plan

challenges.intro_fact: Today is the International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies. Air pollution is often invisible, but it has real, measurable effects on health, in Ireland and worldwide.

questions.text: In 2022, Ireland introduced a nationwide ban on which major source of air pollution?
questions.fact: Ireland's nationwide smoky coal ban came into effect in October 2022, prohibiting the sale of bituminous coal, one of the most polluting home heating fuels.

questions.text: According to the WHO, air pollution contributes to roughly how many premature deaths worldwide each year?
questions.fact: The WHO estimates that air pollution contributes to around 7 million premature deaths worldwide every year, making it one of the biggest environmental health risks globally.

questions.text: The EU's revised Air Quality Directive, agreed in 2024, tightens pollution limits to align more closely with what?
questions.fact: The EU's revised Ambient Air Quality Directive brings legal pollution limits closer to World Health Organization guidelines, with member states required to meet the new standards by 2030.

challenges.action_intro: What you burn at home has a direct effect on the air your neighbours breathe.

actions.title: Check if smoky coal or turf is legal to burn in your area
actions.desc: Rules have been tightening across Ireland, a quick check avoids an unknowing breach.

actions.title: Get your solid fuel stove serviced
actions.desc: A poorly maintained stove burns less efficiently and produces more smoke.

challenges.resources: Ireland solid fuel regulations: gov.ie | WHO air quality: who.int | EU Air Quality Directive: environment.ec.europa.eu

challenges.intro_fact: Autumn is when Ireland's starlings begin gathering into huge, swirling murmurations at dusk, one of the most striking wildlife spectacles you can see close to home.

questions.text: Where in Ireland is one of the best-known places to see huge starling murmurations in autumn and winter?
questions.fact: Lough Ennell in Co. Westmeath is one of Ireland's best-known spots for starling murmurations, where birds can gather by the tens of thousands as the light fades each evening.

questions.text: Many of the starlings seen in Ireland during autumn and winter have travelled from where?
questions.fact: Ireland's winter starling flocks are boosted by migrants arriving from Britain, Scandinavia and eastern Europe, seeking Ireland's comparatively mild winter climate.

questions.text: Why do starlings form huge, swirling murmurations in the sky?
options: For safety in numbers against predators like falcons
questions.fact: Murmurations are thought to be a defence strategy, confusing predators like peregrine falcons by moving as one huge, unpredictable shape.

challenges.action_intro: Autumn is one of the best times of year to notice wildlife on your doorstep.

actions.title: Watch for a murmuration at dusk this month
actions.desc: Starlings gather at reliable roost sites just before sunset. BirdWatch Ireland lists known spots.
actions.carbon: Builds appreciation and awareness of local biodiversity

actions.title: Record a wildlife sighting on a citizen science app
actions.desc: Apps like iNaturalist or BirdTrack let you log what you see, and the data genuinely helps researchers.
actions.carbon: Supports species and seasonal monitoring data

challenges.resources: BirdWatch Ireland: birdwatchireland.ie | iNaturalist: inaturalist.org | National Biodiversity Data Centre: biodiversityireland.ie

challenges.intro_fact: It's easy to assume food miles are the biggest issue with what we eat. The reality is a bit more surprising.

questions.text: Which of these is actually in season in Ireland during September?
questions.fact: September is peak season for Irish apples and blackberries, along with produce like kale, leeks and the main potato harvest.

questions.text: According to a major 2018 global food study, what share of the average food product's carbon footprint comes from transport?
questions.fact: Transport typically makes up less than 10% of a food product's carbon footprint on average, globally. What you eat usually matters far more than how far it travelled.

questions.text: Roughly how many tonnes of food waste does the EU generate every year, according to Eurostat?
questions.fact: The EU generates an estimated 59 million tonnes of food waste every year, a huge amount considering how much energy, land and water go into producing it.

challenges.action_intro: Eating what's actually in season locally is one of the simplest food swaps there is.

actions.title: Add one seasonal Irish item to your shop this week
actions.desc: Look for Irish apples, blackberries or kale instead of imported alternatives, often cheaper too.

actions.title: Check the origin label before you buy fruit and veg
actions.desc: Only takes a second, and builds the habit of noticing where your food comes from.

challenges.resources: Bord Bia seasonal produce: bordbia.ie | Our World in Data food footprint: ourworldindata.org | Eurostat food waste: ec.europa.eu/eurostat

challenges.intro_fact: Today is World Suicide Prevention Day. If you or someone you know is struggling, the Samaritans (116 123, free, 24/7) and Pieta House (1800 247 247) are there to help, any time, day or night. Time in nature is one small, evidence-backed way to support your own mental wellbeing.

questions.text: Research consistently links time spent in green space with what?
questions.fact: Multiple studies link time in green space with lower stress and improved mood, even short walks in a park or near trees show measurable effects.

questions.text: What is the name of the Samaritans' free, 24-hour helpline number in Ireland?
questions.fact: Samaritans Ireland can be reached free, any time, day or night, on 116 123. Pieta House is also available on 1800 247 247.

questions.text: Group nature activities, like community walks or gardening, are linked with what wellbeing benefit, beyond the exercise itself?
options: Reduced feelings of loneliness and stronger social connection
questions.fact: Group nature activities are linked with reduced loneliness and stronger social connection, and connection is one of the most protective factors for mental health.

challenges.action_intro: Small, regular things help: connection, nature and knowing where to turn if things get hard.

actions.title: Reach out to check in with someone today
actions.desc: A short message or call to someone you haven't spoken to in a while can matter more than you think.

actions.title: Take a 15-minute walk somewhere green
actions.desc: Doesn't need to be long or far. A local park, riverside path, or stretch of coast all count.

challenges.resources: Samaritans Ireland: 116 123 (free, 24/7) | Pieta House: 1800 247 247 | Mental Health Ireland: mentalhealthireland.ie

challenges.intro_fact: Ireland was ahead of the curve on plastic policy once before. The EU is now trying to catch the rest of the continent up.

questions.text: Ireland introduced one of the world's first plastic bag levies in 2002. What effect did it have on plastic bag use?
options: A slight increase, as people bought more bags
It was reversed within a year
questions.fact: Ireland's plastic bag levy, introduced in 2002, led to a roughly 90% drop in plastic bag use almost immediately, and is often cited internationally as an early success story.

questions.text: Since July 2021, the EU's Single-Use Plastics Directive has banned which of these products?
questions.fact: Since July 2021, the EU has banned single-use plastic cutlery, straws, plates and several other items where affordable non-plastic alternatives exist.

questions.text: Globally, what share of all plastic ever produced has actually been recycled?
questions.fact: Only around 9% of all plastic ever produced has been recycled. Most has ended up in landfill, incinerated, or in the environment.

challenges.action_intro: The EU is chipping away at single-use plastic, but individual habits still matter.

actions.title: Refuse single-use cutlery or straws this week
actions.desc: Say no when offered, or carry a small reusable set. Adds up over hundreds of takeaways a year.

actions.title: Do one plastic-free grocery shop
actions.desc: Choose loose fruit and veg, and packaging-free options where you can find them.

challenges.resources: EU Single-Use Plastics Directive: environment.ec.europa.eu | Irish plastic bag levy history: gov.ie | Plastic Free July resources

challenges.intro_fact: This year's UN climate summit, COP31, is approaching. Behind the headlines, the real fight is often about money: who pays, and how much.

questions.text: According to McKinsey analysis, roughly how much global investment is needed every year to reach net zero by 2050?
questions.fact: McKinsey estimates reaching net zero by 2050 will require around $9.2 trillion in investment every single year, and neither governments nor private investors are currently deploying capital anywhere near that fast.

questions.text: This year's UN climate summit, COP31, is due to take place in which country?
questions.fact: COP31 is scheduled to take place in Antalya, Turkey, continuing the annual UN climate negotiations that began with the Paris Agreement in 2015.

questions.text: Ireland's carbon tax revenue is required by law to be used for what?
options: General government spending, with no restrictions
Ring-fenced for things like retrofits, welfare compensation and the Just Transition
Paid directly to fossil fuel companies as compensation
questions.fact: Irish law requires carbon tax revenue to be ring-fenced, funding home energy retrofits, welfare measures to protect lower-income households, and the Just Transition Fund.

challenges.action_intro: Climate finance can feel abstract, but it shapes what gets built, and where.

actions.title: Look up what Ireland's carbon tax actually funds
actions.desc: A few minutes on gov.ie shows exactly where the ring-fenced revenue goes.
actions.carbon: Builds understanding of national climate policy

actions.title: Follow COP31 coverage as it happens
actions.desc: Following even a few days of real coverage builds a much clearer picture than headlines alone.

challenges.resources: Ireland carbon tax: gov.ie | COP31 official site: unfccc.int | McKinsey net zero financing report

challenges.intro_fact: 2026 is an unusual year in global environmental diplomacy: climate, biodiversity and land negotiations are all happening in the same year.

questions.text: The '30x30' target agreed under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework aims to protect what?
questions.fact: The 30x30 target, agreed at COP15 in 2022, commits countries to protecting 30% of the world's land and sea by 2030, one of the most ambitious global conservation goals ever set.

questions.text: Which international treaty, adopted alongside the UNFCCC at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit, focuses specifically on protecting nature and species?
questions.fact: The Convention on Biological Diversity was adopted at the same 1992 Rio Earth Summit as the UNFCCC, but focuses specifically on protecting species, ecosystems and genetic diversity.

questions.text: In 2019, Ireland became one of the first countries to declare what, alongside a climate emergency?
questions.fact: Ireland declared a biodiversity emergency in 2019, one of the first countries in the world to do so, recognising nature loss as a crisis on the same scale as climate change.

challenges.action_intro: Nature negotiations get far less attention than climate ones, but the stakes are just as high.

actions.title: Learn one action from Ireland's National Biodiversity Action Plan
actions.desc: A few minutes on npws.ie shows practical steps happening at national level.
actions.carbon: Builds understanding of national biodiversity policy

actions.title: Support a local biodiversity project
actions.desc: From community gardens to local Tidy Towns biodiversity initiatives, small local efforts add up.
actions.carbon: Supports local habitat and species protection

challenges.resources: CBD official site: cbd.int | NPWS: npws.ie | Ireland's National Biodiversity Action Plan: gov.ie

challenges.intro_fact: Today marks World Ozone Day. The story of the ozone layer is one of the rare cases where the world acted fast, together, and it worked, mostly.

questions.text: The Montreal Protocol, signed in 1987, tackled ozone depletion by phasing out which chemicals?
questions.fact: The Montreal Protocol phased out CFCs, once common in fridges, air conditioning and aerosol sprays, and is widely regarded as one of the most successful environmental agreements in history.

questions.text: By when is the ozone layer expected to fully recover over most of the world, according to the UN?
questions.fact: The UN projects the ozone layer will fully recover by 2040 over most of the world, by 2045 over the Arctic, and by 2066 over Antarctica, where the damage was worst.

questions.text: A mysterious rise in banned CFC-11 emissions after 2013 was traced largely to illegal production in which country?
questions.fact: Investigations traced a rise in banned CFC-11 emissions largely to illegal production in China, a reminder that even a strong global ban needs ongoing enforcement.

challenges.action_intro: The ozone story shows that global environmental problems can be solved, and also that they need to stay solved.

actions.title: Check your fridge and AC unit are properly serviced
actions.desc: Older units can still leak banned refrigerant gases if damaged or poorly maintained.
actions.carbon: Prevents leaks of ozone-depleting and warming gases

actions.title: Learn one thing about an environmental success story
actions.desc: The ozone layer is proof that global cooperation works, a genuinely hopeful climate story to share.

challenges.resources: UNEP ozone recovery assessment: unep.org | Montreal Protocol: ozone.unep.org

challenges.intro_fact: Climate Carnival brings climate leaders and changemakers together in Stradbally this week, right in the middle of European Mobility Week, Europe's longest-running sustainable transport campaign.

questions.text: European Mobility Week, one of the longest-running sustainable transport campaigns in the world, has run annually since when?
questions.fact: European Mobility Week has run annually since 2002, making it one of the longest-standing EU campaigns promoting walking, cycling and public transport over car use.

questions.text: Roughly how many towns and cities across Europe take part in European Mobility Week each year?
options: Just a handful of capital cities
questions.fact: Over 3,000 towns and cities across Europe take part in European Mobility Week each year, organising local events, car-free days and new infrastructure launches.

questions.text: Roughly what share of car trips in the EU are under 5 km, short enough for many people to realistically walk or cycle instead?
questions.fact: Roughly half of all car trips in the EU are under 5 km, distances many people could walk, cycle or take public transport instead.

actions.title: Swap one short car trip for walking or cycling this week
actions.desc: If it's under 5km, there's a good chance you could walk or cycle it just as easily.

actions.title: Check out Climate Carnival or a local Mobility Week event near you
actions.desc: Local events often include free bike checks, taster cycling sessions or public transport demos.
actions.carbon: Builds engagement with local low-carbon transport options

challenges.resources: European Mobility Week: mobilityweek.eu | Climate Carnival: climatecarnival.ie | Transport for Ireland: transportforireland.ie

challenges.intro_fact: Today is World Bamboo Day. Bamboo is establishing itself as a credible low-carbon alternative to wood, plastic and even concrete, and its climate potential remains widely underestimated.

questions.text: Bamboo absorbs how much more CO2 than European broadleaf forests, according to research cited in a 2026 article?
questions.fact: Bamboo absorbs 30 to 40% more CO2 than European broadleaf forests, while releasing around 30% more oxygen, yet its climate potential remains widely underestimated.

questions.text: France's start-up Horizom is developing bamboo plantations, with plans to reach how many hectares by 2050?
questions.fact: French start-up Horizom already manages 460 hectares of bamboo across 34 departments, with plans to develop 50,000 hectares by 2050, part of a growing European bamboo industry.

questions.text: Unlike trees, bamboo is technically a type of what, which is part of why it grows so fast?
questions.fact: Bamboo is a grass, not a tree, which is part of why it can be harvested annually from around the fifth year after planting, one of the fastest renewable materials available.

challenges.action_intro: You've probably used bamboo without realising how much potential it has.

actions.title: Try one bamboo product swap
actions.desc: Toothbrushes, socks and kitchen utensils are common starting points. Watch out for bamboo viscose fabric, it's heavily processed and loses much of the benefit.

actions.title: Look for FSC or verified sourcing on bamboo products
actions.desc: Not all bamboo is grown or processed responsibly. A recognised certification is a good way to check.

challenges.intro_fact: Today is the International Day of Peace. Climate change is increasingly a driver of conflict and instability, but there's a deeper unfairness underneath it: the people who did the least to cause it are often hit hardest.

questions.text: Under its International Climate Finance Roadmap, what did Ireland commit to by 2025?
options: At least double its climate finance to developing countries, to around €225 million a year
Join the Loss and Damage Fund as the only EU contributor
questions.fact: Ireland committed to at least double its climate finance to developing countries, to support countries most affected by a crisis they did little to cause.

questions.text: At COP27 and COP28, countries agreed to set up a fund to help vulnerable nations cope with climate damage they didn't cause. What is it called?
questions.fact: Countries agreed to a Loss and Damage Fund, channelling money from richer nations, which bear the most historical responsibility, to poorer countries facing the worst impacts.

questions.text: According to IEA analysis, how much more CO2 does the world's top 1% of emitters produce than the bottom 1%?
questions.fact: The top 1% of emitters produce over 1,000 times more CO2 than the bottom 1%, one of the starkest measures of climate inequality.

challenges.action_intro: Climate justice can feel like a huge, distant topic, but there are still concrete things you can do.

actions.title: Learn where your bank invests your money
actions.desc: A quick look at your bank's climate policy tells you a lot.

actions.title: Support Irish Aid or a climate justice charity
actions.desc: Groups like Trócaire work directly with communities facing the worst impacts.
actions.carbon: Supports climate adaptation in vulnerable regions

challenges.resources: Irish Aid: irishaid.ie | UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund: unfccc.int | Trócaire: trocaire.org

challenges.intro_fact: Today is World Car Free Day. Ireland's transport emissions are growing faster than almost anywhere else in Europe, and cars are the main reason why.

questions.text: What share of Ireland's transport emissions comes from road use (cars, vans, trucks)?
questions.fact: Roughly 95% of Ireland's transport emissions come from road use, compared to an EU average of about 75%.

questions.text: In 2022, Irish transport emissions grew 6.7%. How did that compare to the EU?
options: Ireland grew slower than the EU average
More than double the EU average of 2.7%
Both fell by the same amount
questions.fact: Irish transport emissions rose 6.7% in 2022, more than double the EU's average increase of 2.7% that year.

questions.text: On average, how much of a car's life is spent parked and unused?
questions.fact: Studies suggest the average car sits parked and unused around 95% of the time.

challenges.intro_fact: It's European Mobility Week. Public transport use in Ireland is growing, but the network is close to full at peak times, and Irish rail lags far behind the rest of Europe on electrification.

questions.text: How much did TFI network journeys grow in 2025 compared to 2024?
questions.fact: TFI journeys grew about 6% in 2025, and Local Link rural journeys grew even faster, up 19%, though capacity is now near its limit at peak times.

questions.text: How does electrification of Ireland's rail network compare to the EU average?
options: Ireland is close to average, at 50%
Ireland is far behind, at just 2.6% versus an EU average of about 57%
questions.fact: Just 2.6% of Irish railway lines were electrified as of 2022, one of the lowest rates in Europe.

questions.text: Roughly what share of global energy-related CO2 emissions comes from transport?
questions.fact: Transport accounts for roughly a quarter of global energy-related CO2 emissions, with road vehicles the largest share.

challenges.action_intro: European Mobility Week runs all week, a good excuse to try something new.

actions.title: Try a Leap Card or local transport app for a week

challenges.intro_fact: It's International Happiness at Work Week. Sustainability and workplace wellbeing turn out to be more connected than you'd think, from how we get to work to how work itself is structured.

questions.text: What is Ireland's tax-free scheme that helps employees buy a bike for commuting called?
questions.fact: The Cycle to Work Scheme lets employees buy a bike and safety equipment tax-free through their employer, making active commuting cheaper.

questions.text: Trials of the four-day work week across Europe (UK and others) found what effect?
options: Improved wellbeing and productivity, with most companies keeping it
questions.fact: Multiple European four-day work week trials found improved employee wellbeing and stable or improved productivity, with the vast majority of participating companies choosing to continue.

questions.text: Research from the University of East Anglia found that switching from driving to walking or cycling to work led to what?
options: A measurable improvement in mental wellbeing
questions.fact: People who switched from driving to active commuting reported measurably better mental wellbeing than those who kept driving.

challenges.action_intro: The trick to a habit that lasts is tying it to something you already do every day.

actions.title: Suggest a green idea at work this week
actions.desc: A bike rack, a recycling audit, small changes that also boost morale.

actions.title: Try one active or public transport commute this week
actions.desc: Even once counts.

challenges.intro_fact: Recycle Week starts today. Ireland's waste system has changed hugely in the past 20 years, from open landfill to a much more tracked system, but small mistakes still send good recycling to waste.

questions.text: How many active landfill sites does Ireland have today, down from around 125 in the year 2000?
questions.fact: Ireland went from around 125 landfill sites in 2000 to just 3 by 2021, as part of the EU's Landfill Directive.

questions.text: On average, how much less greenhouse gas do recycled materials produce compared to virgin (new) materials?
questions.fact: Recycled materials produce roughly 40% less emissions on average, by avoiding landfill emissions and the energy needed to extract and process new raw materials.

questions.text: Under EU law, what recycling rate must member states hit for municipal waste by 2035?
questions.fact: The EU Waste Framework Directive requires member states to recycle at least 65% of municipal waste by 2035.

challenges.action_intro: Recycle Week is a good nudge to double-check you're getting it right.

actions.desc: Two minutes now saves a contaminated bin later.

actions.title: Make sure recycling is clean, dry and loose
actions.desc: Food residue and bagged items are common causes of rejected batches.

challenges.intro_fact: Ireland's Deposit Return Scheme has been running for a while now. If you're still binning your bottles and cans, you're leaving money behind, literally.

questions.text: When did Ireland's Deposit Return Scheme (Re-Turn) launch?
questions.fact: Ireland's Deposit Return Scheme launched on 1 February 2024, adding a small refundable deposit to most plastic bottles and cans.

questions.text: How much is the deposit on a large plastic bottle (500ml or over)?
questions.fact: Containers under 500ml carry a 15 cent deposit; containers 500ml and over carry a 25 cent deposit, refunded when you return the empty container.

questions.text: The EU's Single-Use Plastics Directive requires member states to separately collect what percentage of plastic bottles by 2029?
questions.fact: The EU requires a 90% separate collection rate for plastic bottles by 2029, which is why deposit schemes like Re-Turn have spread across Europe.

challenges.intro_fact: Today marks the UN's International Day of Awareness of Food Loss and Waste. Nearly a third of all food produced worldwide is never eaten, and Irish households throw out more than most people realise.

questions.text: Roughly how much food waste does the average person in Ireland produce per year?
questions.fact: The average person in Ireland produces around 162 kg of food waste a year, roughly 444 kg per household.

questions.text: Roughly what share of all food produced worldwide is wasted?
questions.fact: Roughly one-third of all food produced worldwide is wasted, along with all the water, energy, land and labour that went into it.

questions.text: What share of global greenhouse gas emissions does the global food system account for?
questions.fact: The global food system, farming, transport, processing and waste combined, accounts for around 34% of global emissions.

challenges.action_intro: Every kilo of food saved is roughly 3 kg of CO2 avoided, composting the rest matters too.

actions.desc: Composting cuts food waste's climate impact by more than 90% versus landfill.

challenges.intro_fact: Recycle Week wraps up today. One of the most common recycling myths is hiding in plain sight, on the label of the bottle in your hand.

questions.text: What accounting trick lets a company label a product 'recycled' even if it's mostly new (virgin) plastic?
questions.fact: Mass balance accounting lets a manufacturer average a small amount of recycled material across an entire production system, then label individual products as recycled, even if the one in your hand is around 95% virgin material.

questions.text: What EU regulation, updated in 2026, allows this mass balance approach to continue?
options: The Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR)
questions.fact: The EU's Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation legalises mass balance accounting for recycled content claims in 2026, rather than closing the loophole.

questions.text: What's the simplest rule of thumb for what belongs in an Irish recycling bin?
questions.fact: Irish recycling guidance boils down to 'clean, dry and loose.' Food residue, wet cardboard and bagged items are common causes of a batch being rejected.

challenges.action_intro: Recycling still matters, just don't let a label do your thinking for you.

actions.title: Choose products with less packaging, not just recyclable packaging
actions.desc: Less packaging beats recyclable packaging every time.
actions.carbon: Cuts packaging waste at the source

actions.title: Rinse and dry your recycling before it goes out
actions.desc: A few seconds under the tap stops a whole batch getting contaminated.
